Thin data: 3 of 6 key inputs were sourced (missing: TUSC pts scored, TUSC pts allowed, TUSC lineup rating or past seasons), so league averages filled the gaps. It was logged as a no-data call: graded and learned from, never offered as a bet.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Pioneers came in with a league-average attack and a league-average defense (no scoring on file: rated at the league average), worth about 14 and 14 games of evidence. Projected to score 69.7, they scored 50 (−19.7 points, 28% under); projected to allow 64.2, they allowed 79 (+14.8 points, 23% over).

Eagles came in with a 10% below average attack and a 6% leakier than average defense (0-5, 58 scored and 81.2 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 167 and 170 games of evidence. Projected to score 64.2, they scored 79 (+14.8 points, 23% over); projected to allow 69.7, they allowed 50 (−19.7 points, 28% under).

The bigger miss was Pioneers' scoring (-19.7 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 129 against 133.9 projected (-4.9), about the 36th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14).

Margin: Eagles by 29 against Pioneers by 5.6 projected, about the 99th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±13).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (TUSC pts scored, TUSC pts allowed, TUSC lineup rating or past seasons); there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.940 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +35.9 points. It counts toward NCAAW scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections (it's how teams with no standings on the routes build a record of their own).

Across 762 graded NCAAW games the algo now scales scoring ×0.975 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: Eagles attack ×1.034, defense ×0.987 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 34.6 points), no bet.
